newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JUNE 23.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
-- A visiting World Bank mission agreed with Bulgaria on the introduction of a temporary tax on grain exports until the year-end, which will ease the path for World Bank loans.
The World Bank team visited the Balkan state to ensure that the new reformist government will continue the fast pace of structural reform started by the interim cabinet in March.
-- Police raided the offices of the private Slavyani bank, in receivership since September 1996, in search of evidence of suspected extending of uncollateralised credits.
-- Bulgaria lifted price controls on 15 basic foods as part of further price liberalisation required by the International Monetary Fund.
Under the new mechanism, flexible prices will be negotiated between producers and traders, and retailers should put stickers on the goods showing the price agreed between producers and traders.
-- Sofia City Court court is expected to rule on July 4 on an insolvency case against the private Slavyani Bank filed by the central bank in October 1996.

-- The parliament tentatively approved the 1997 state budget proposed by the cabinet. Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said this was a budget of harsh financial restrictions and was reflecting the grim condition of the country's economy.
The parliament is expected to pass the 1997 budget law until July 1, when Bulgaria launches a tough self-regulating monetary mechanism known as currency board.
-- The state Zemedelie agricultural fund extended subsidies of 1.5 billion levs ($882,000) to support this year's wheat harvesting. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
